subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error fix, or a documented decision that current coarse scopes are the intended core boundary?
rationale: The report is valid enough to keep open, but choosing default exclusions and protected backup contents affects restore completeness and security, so automation should not choose the final product policy while a linked PR is already under review.

options.title: Narrow and review native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving proof, protected-path semantics, external-asset behavior, and upgrade safety.

options.title: Ship minimal reliability first
options.body: Fix the archive path to complete or fail clearly with progress or size guidance while deferring smart/custom exclusions to a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Defer core scope expansion
options.body: Document current core backup limits and point users to plugin or workaround options only if maintainers decide native exclusions are outside core for now.

recommendation.title: Narrow and review native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a replacement as the implementation path after resolving proof, protected-path semantics, external-asset behavior, and upgrade safety.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a restore-safety and CLI product-boundary decision, and steipete has the strongest recent current-main routing signal among the likely owners.
